PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-06-18
40F, outpatient visit for a routine check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. She reports feeling generally well. Over the past several weeks she has had intermittent joint aches in the hands with mild morning stiffness and a sun-sensitive facial rash, prompting workup today. Patient denies depression. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. She works as a paralegal, mostly seated. Appetite is good and sleep is adequate. Lives with her spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 118/74, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 152 lb, BMI 25.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: mild redness over sun-exposed skin of the face.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: mild tenderness at the small joints of the hands, no effusion, full range of motion.
Skin: faint sunburn-like redness over the cheeks.
Labs (this week): A1c 6.0%, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, eGFR 78 mL/min/1.73m2, ANA negative, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 48 mg/g.

A/P:
1. Chronic kidney disease stage 2, stable. Renal function stable on today's labs. Continue to avoid nephrotoxic agents; acetaminophen acceptable for comfort. Repeat renal panel in 6 months.
2. Rule out lupus; ANA negative. Facial redness fits sun exposure and the joint aches fit repetitive hand use; no further autoimmune testing or rheumatology referral needed. Advised strict sun protection.
3. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
4. Health maintenance: cervical screening up to date; mammography discussed. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall.

Return in 3 months, sooner if the rash spreads or new joint swelling develops.
